title: Assembly and Characterization of Biomolecular Memristors Consisting of Ion Channel-doped Lipid Membranes
protocol: Select suitable, undamaged measuring/mixing glassware for use.
Handle glassware carefully to avoid damage.
Wear latex or nitrile gloves to avoid contaminating the glassware with residues from fingertips and to protect your skin.
Clean chosen glassware thoroughly using detergent solution and water by scrubbing until clean and all residues are removed.
Rinse thoroughly with tap water.
Rinse thoroughly with deionized (DI) water.
Place on drying rack to air dry.
Optional: Rinse the cleaned glassware with isopropyl alcohol (IPA, 99.5%) and place under vacuum to evaporate all residual IPA.
Remove from vacuum chamber and place in a clean environment.
Purchase sterile small glass vials and safe-lock tubes for materials preparation and sample storage.
Wear latex or nitrile gloves.
Select an appropriate and clean glass container.
Prepare 50 mL of aqueous buffer solution containing 500 mM sodium chloride (KCl) and 10 mM MOPS at pH 7.0.
Dispense 1.86378 g of KCl onto clean weighing paper using a digital, high precision mass balance and a clean spatula.
Weigh 0.10463 g of MOPS and add to the glass container containing KCl.
Add 50 mL of DI water to the glass container and vortex thoroughly until KCl and MOPS are completely dissolved.
Store the buffer solution at room temperature for use when needed.
Dissolve 5 mg of DPhPC or BTLE lipids in 1 mL of chloroform in a 5 mL sterile glass vial.
While gently swirling, evaporate the chloroform under a gentle stream of dry nitrogen until a lipid film remains at the bottom of the vial.
Place the vial containing the lipid film under vacuum for 10-12 h to allow for complete removal of residual chloroform.
Remove the vial from the vacuum chamber and rehydrate the lipid film by adding 10 mL of the aqueous buffer solution prepared in Step 2.
Freeze the lipid suspension six times at -20°C to facilitate multilamellar liposome assembly.
Thaw the mixture at room temperature.
Extrude the liposome solution by forcing it through a 0.1 μm pore diameter track-etched membrane using an extruder.
Repeat the extrusion process eleven times in immediate succession.
Store the liposome suspension at 4°C and use within one week of preparation.
Warm up the extruder to 45-50°C for BTLE liposomes.
Place the closed suspension vial into a bath sonicator at 55°C for approximately fifteen minutes to prepare hydrated BTLE liposome suspensions directly.
Dissolve alamethicin peptides in ethanol to a final concentration of 2.5 mg/mL.
Vortex briefly to mix well.
Store the stock solution in freezer at -20 °C.
Mix 99 μL of solution “A” with 1 μL of alamethicin stock solution to achieve a final alamethicin concentration of 13 μM in the liposome suspension.
Vortex to mix well.
Refer to the resulting peptide-liposome solution as “B”.
Mix 117 μL of solution “A” with 10 μL of solution B to achieve a final alamethicin concentration of 1 μM.
Vortex to mix well.
Refer to the resulting solution as “C”.
Store solutions B and C at 4 °C for use as needed.
Using a digital, high precision mass balance and a clean spatula, add 0.5 g of agarose powder to a weighing paper.
Transfer weighed agarose to a 100-mL clean glass beaker.
Add 50 mL of DI water to the agarose in the beaker.
Place a stirring magnet inside the glass beaker and place it on a stirring hot plate.
Stirring, bring the mixture to a boil until agarose is completely dissolved.
Remove the beaker from the hot plate.
Let the mixture cool to room temperature.
Store at 4 °C for use when needed.
Before using again, re-melt the agarose by heating with a hot plate or microwave.
Cut a 12 x 12 x 12 mm acrylic cube from a larger 12 mm thick acrylic sheet using a band saw.
Mill a 12 mm diameter hole to a depth of 8-12 mm in the acrylic tube.
Cut two pieces (75 mm) of silver wires (125 μm-diameter) using scissors.
Melt one end of each silver wire to form small spherical balls (around 250 μm in diameter) using an open-flame lighter.
Immerse the ball ends in bleach for 1-2 h to create a silver-silver chloride (Ag/AgCl) coating.
Remove both wires from bleach and rinse thoroughly with DI water, then place aside on a clean lint-free wipe.
Dip the ball ends into molten agarose gel to create a thin layer.
Split a 10-cm long, 1/0.58 OD/ID mm borosilicate glass capillary into two 5 cm capillaries using a glass cutter.
Insert one of the glass capillaries into an electrode holder.
Feed one Ag/AgCl wire into the glass capillary inserted in the holder.
Feed the other Ag/AgCl wire into the second glass capillary.
Mount the second glass capillary to a glass micropipette holder.
Place a 1 mm thick, 25 x 75 mm glass slide on the stage of an inverted microscope.
Dispense a few drops of hexadecane oil onto the center of the glass slide.
Position the oil reservoir directly onto the oil on the glass slide.
Completely fill the oil reservoir with hexadecane oil.
Connect the electrode holder to the headstage of a current amplifier.
Mount the headstage on a micromanipulator to minimize electrode length and electrical noise.
Mount the glass micropipette holder with the second Ag/AgCl wire onto another micromanipulator.
Position the electrodes such that the agarose coated tips of the Ag/AgCl wires are fully submerged into the oil reservoir at a similar vertical plane.
Align the two electrodes and separate them by a few millimeters.
Create a Ground bus by threading a screw into the anti-vibration table.
Connect the screw to an earth ground with a conductive wire.
Connect the microscope stage to the Ground bus.
Place a Faraday cage over the experimental setup.
Electrically connect the Faraday cage to the Ground bus.
Machine an aluminum heating shell for the oil reservoir to fit snugly.
Leave an opening at the bottom of the shell for viewing through the inverted microscope.
Place a 30 x 30 mm resistive polyimide flexible heating element underneath the aluminum shell.
Insert an insulating PDMS wafer beneath the heater.
Position the thermocouple into the oil phase without touching Ag/AgCl wires.
Connect the thermocouple wires to a thermocouple data acquisition board.
Record temperature using custom programming software.
Write an On-Off proportional integral (PI) feedback temperature control code.
Power on computer(s), microscope, function generator, current amplifier, and low-noise data acquisition systems.
Set the front panel display and source-measurement Mode dials to VHOLD/IHOLD and V-CLAMP, respectively.
Set the Lowpass Bessel Filter to 1 kHz on the front panel.
Set the Output Gain to 0.5.
Set the Configuration to WHOLE CELL β = 1.
Double-click on the icon of the desktop software to initialize it.
Click Configuration | Digitizer to open the Digitizer dialog.
Click the Change button in the Digitizer dialog.
Select the appropriate digitizer from the Digitizer Type list.
Click the Scan button to detect the digitizer.
Click OK to exit the Change Digitizer dialog.
Click OK to exit the Digitizer dialog.
Click Configure | Lab Bench.
Set the scale factor to 0.0005 V/pA in the Input Signals tab of the Lab Bench.
Deposit 200 nL of aqueous lipid solution “A” onto the ends of each Ag/AgCl wire under oil using a micropipette.
Bring the droplets into contact and press the ZAP button on the front panel of the amplifier to coalesce the droplets.
Set source-measurement mode dial to TRACK.
Change the front panel display dial to VTRACK.
Turn the PIPETTER OFFSET dial until meter reads 0 mV and is stable.
Return the source-measurement mode dial to V-CLAMP.
Return the front panel display dial to VHOLD/IHOLD.
Release the droplets by moving the electrodes vertically out of the oil phase.
Re-submerge and position the electrodes in oil.
Use a micropipette to deposit 200 nL of lipid solution “A” on each of the wires.
Wait for 3-5 minutes to allow spontaneous lipid monolayer assembly at each water/oil interface.
Lower the electrodes until they barely touch the bottom of the oil reservoir.
Move the electrodes horizontally to bring the droplets into contact.
Record the lipid bilayer formation using a 10 Hz, 10 mV triangular waveform voltage from a function generator connected to the patch clamp amplifier.
Observe the growth in peak-to-peak current amplitude during lipid bilayer formation.
Using a function generator, apply a voltage waveform to an alamethicin-free lipid membrane assembled with droplets of solution “A”.
Record the induced current response across multiple frequencies.
Measure the size of the interfacial lipid bilayer by either measuring its diameter or recording the peak-to-peak current amplitude resulting from a 10 Hz, 10 mV triangular wave.
Remove droplets that contain no alamethicin.
Add new aqueous droplets using solution “C” and form a lipid bilayer.
Adjust contact between droplets to ensure the bilayer has a similar area as previously measured.
Subtract current recorded in step 14.2.2 from current recorded in step 14.2.7.
Plot the induced current versus applied voltage for each frequency and waveform to obtain the "pinched hysteresis" memristive response.
Generate voltage pulses with specific high and low amplitudes, ON time, and OFF time using custom programming software and analog voltage source.
Record the current in response to applied pulses.
Apply a low-pass filter with appropriate passband to remove capacitive spikes.
